description: Tawhid: the oneness of God (Allah), worshipping Allah alone, God's uniqueness, the meaning of the word 'Allah'.

documents.text: Tawhid means the absolute oneness of God (Allah). It is the foundation of Islamic belief. "Say, He is Allah, [who is] One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent." (112:1-4). "And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful." (2:163).

Tawhid is not only believing that one God exists; it also means directing all worship to Allah alone. "And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, There is no deity except Me, so worship Me." (21:25). "It is You we worship and You we ask for help." (1:5). Associating partners with Allah in worship (shirk) is the opposite of Tawhid.

Tawhid includes affirming that nothing resembles Allah: "There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing." (42:11). Allah is not described with human limitations and has no physical equal or likeness in creation.

"Allah" is the Arabic word for God, the One God. It is not the name of a separate or exclusively Arab deity; Arabic-speaking Jews and Christians also use the word Allah for God. The Qur'an instructs Muslims to say to the People of the Book: "our God and your God is one." (29:46). Presenting "Allah" as a foreign or tribal god is a common cross-cultural misunderstanding.
